scope: All 31 unmatched names in the previous handoff; bounded exact-object reuse and selected new primary-source searches, not internet-wide exhaustion. Search results are candidate leads, not licenses verified for import. Imported Sketchfab assets have separate detail-API license snapshots.

items.name: Proton volume
items.decision: Charge radius is not a hard solid boundary. Existing Length probability/particle diagrams and newly synthesized shells are ineligible; no new search of the same dead end.
items.prior_blocker: Quantum charge-density extent is not a uniquely bounded solid body; use a labeled distribution visualization, not a solid mesh-volume claim.

items.name: Hydrogen atom volume
items.decision: Bohr-radius volume is a convention. Existing procedural Length orbitals are not qualifying imported geometry; no stand-in sphere added.
items.prior_blocker: The Bohr-radius-derived effective volume is a convention, not a hard atomic boundary; any shell must be labeled as a probability/scale illustration.

items.name: Water molecule volume
items.decision: Existing archived H2O GLB is a ball illustration with several overlapping/disjoint atom shells. The strict helper rejects multiple shells; no matching electron-density or van-der-Waals volume boundary is established. Unlike a whole-object illustration, atom balls would imply an unsupported molecular boundary.
items.prior_blocker: Molecular volume depends on the chosen electron-density or van-der-Waals boundary; no licensed exact source geometry matching the current definition is registered.

items.name: SARS-CoV-2 virion volume
items.calibration: explicit equivalent-volume-span illustration; not enclosed-volume calibrated
items.prior_blocker_resolution: The current brief explicitly permits existing public models with an equivalent-volume-span fallback. Notes disclose which volume is not measured; sugar scan instead has a closed exterior shell audit.

items.name: Influenza virion volume
items.calibration: explicit equivalent-volume-span illustration; not enclosed-volume calibrated

reviewed_alternatives.license: CC BY 4.0 confirmed by university collection page
reviewed_alternatives.decision: ZIP central directories inspected by HTTP range requests; full influenza files are 3ds Max scenes, while the print STL is about 345 MB uncompressed. No model member acquired. NIH supplies a much smaller colored cutaway directly as GLB.
Staged outside the repo and CPU-previewed; generic gray educational surface reads less clearly than the selected NIH colored scientific cutaway. Not bundled.

items.name: Escherichia coli cell volume
items.decision: Existing Length bacterium source explicitly says very generic, and the stored asset has shortened flagella and fails strict topology on a degenerate triangle. New bedonio candidate is labeled E. coli but has no specimen, geometry-creation or upstream provenance beyond a generic organism description. Several search results are duplicate student uploads; no new model selected.
items.prior_blocker: Cell volume varies with strain and growth conditions; require a measured specimen or clearly identified representative cell model.

items.name: Human cell volume
items.decision: Brain_Diagno identifies an epithelial cell made in Blender, without a measured specimen or boundary convention. Existing named cell-type Length assets are authored project geometry, not qualifying external reuse. No one cell type established for the generic 4 pL record.
items.prior_blocker: There is no single typical human-cell geometry; organelle/whole-cell renderings need an explicit cell type, boundary and compatible license.

items.name: Grain of salt volume
items.decision: First-page downloadable CC BY/CC0 results are unrelated mineral collections, food props and kitchen scenes. No single salt-grain scan with defensible source identity found; no reuse of the carbonate sand grain for salt.
items.prior_blocker: The record is a representative spherical approximation; an actual irregular grain would need measured dimensions and matching size provenance.

items.name: Raindrop volume
items.decision: Search results are stylized drops, rain-ring effects and impressions. A pointed teardrop prop would conflict with a free-falling 5 mm spherical approximation; no physical measured drop mesh selected.
items.prior_blocker: The listed 5 mm spherical droplet is a simplifying convention; real falling-drop shape depends on size and airflow.

items.name: Room volume
items.decision: First-page scan leads concern furnished room scenes and scan fragments, without an isolated inside boundary, identified 30 m3 air volume, or small-view exterior readability. No room surface is asserted to be air volume.
items.prior_blocker: A representative interior needs dimensions and a clear wall/ceiling boundary; generic room assets are not calibrated to the selected example.

items.name: Swimming pool
items.decision: Generic pool scenes identify neither a measured 40 m3 water fill nor a controlled basin boundary. Deck and landscaping would dominate the selected span; no water geometry fabricated.
items.prior_blocker: The 40 m^3 observation is water capacity; a pool shell/envelope is not the water volume unless fill level and basin geometry are explicit.

items.name: Apartment
items.decision: Furnished scene leads do not establish a 120 m3 inside-air boundary or attribution for all bundled props. No apartment scene imported as a measured solid.
items.prior_blocker: Representative interior volume needs a dimensioned apartment plan/model matching the record; an attractive room scene is not sufficient.

items.name: Classroom volume
items.decision: Whole furnished classroom scenes/props lack an isolated 150 m3 interior-air boundary; no external mesh or component provenance passed a detailed import review.
items.prior_blocker: Needs room dimensions and an explicit interior-air boundary; generic classroom models may include furniture or omit architectural surfaces.

items.name: Apartment volume
items.decision: Same apartment scene review as Apartment; no calibrated 200 m3 interior-air body or controlled cutaway source selected.
items.prior_blocker: Representative interior-air volume requires a dimensionally controlled plan and a defined inside boundary.

items.name: House interior volume
items.decision: Interior scans/props reviewed above do not establish the selected whole-house air boundary, excluded walls/floors or attic treatment. No envelope box created.
items.prior_blocker: Representative interior volume requires an identified house plan and consistent treatment of floors, walls, attic and excluded spaces.

items.name: Olympic swimming pool
items.decision: First-page open results are an Olympic stadium, swimming animation and unrelated money-bin scene, not an identified dimensioned competition-pool water body.
items.prior_blocker: Capacity depends on the selected competition dimensions and water depth; require a source model or plan matching the cited pool convention.

items.name: Oil tanker cargo volume
items.decision: Search leads include exterior ships and road tankers. No exact vessel cargo-tank capacity or internal tank boundary is documented. Existing Ever Given is a container ship/project-authored illustration, not the same object and not cargo-tank geometry.
items.prior_blocker: Cargo capacity is not hull displacement or outer hull volume; a particular vessel and tank-capacity source are needed.

items.name: Great Pyramid of Giza volume
items.decision: Prior PAPP whole-scene/rights and YouTube photogrammetry decisions were not repeated. New bounded query produced no relevant open scan. No procedural pyramid or whole-plateau volume imported.
items.prior_blocker: The selected value is an approximate geometric envelope (~2.6 million m^3). The CC BY PAPP Sketchfab file describes a watertight whole-plateau bas-relief containing multiple pyramids, Sphinx, causeway and terrain, not an isolated calibrated Khufu mesh. Verify source/dependency rights and isolate the pyramid before considering import.

items.name: Lake Tahoe volume
items.decision: Primary USGS data-download documentation identifies a 10 m bathymetry grid, 3416 by 1992 samples and elevations 1400.017 to 1898.999 m. Its 34.16 km bounding span is about 6.4 times cbrt(151 km3), so a water body retaining physical proportions would exceed the 1.3 display-extent rule. Lake-level/datum, shallow coverage and numerical download review are still needed. No grid acquired or water mesh invented. The single Sketchfab lake lead is not assumed to encode water-column volume.
items.prior_blocker: Water volume requires bathymetry and a defined lake level; surrounding terrain topography alone is not the water body.

items.name: Mount Everest envelope volume
items.decision: Existing Mapzen Length terrain block has an arbitrary rectangular clipping boundary and sea-level base, not the dataset above-surrounding-terrain envelope. Reusing its closed block would falsely count the wrong solid. No new boundary invented.
items.prior_blocker: An above-terrain envelope needs a defined base surface, summit and clipping boundary; ordinary elevation relief is not this volume.

items.name: Earth's oceans
items.decision: NOAA confirms public ETOPO topography/bathymetry. Existing Earth globe depicts the full planet rather than the water column. A physically proportioned global water shell spans roughly a planet diameter while cbrt(ocean volume) is much smaller; no closed water-column extraction, sea-level convention or <=1.3 extent solution completed. No globe incorrectly volume-calibrated as ocean water.
items.prior_blocker: Ocean volume requires a bathymetric water-column calculation and a sea-level/datum convention; a globe or ocean-surface map is not volume geometry.

items.name: Betelgeuse volume
items.decision: The existing nasa-sun-as-betelgeuse Length entry explicitly reuses a recolored Sun, a different object. It is not an exact-object sourced stellar surface under this brief. No new sphere or Sun reuse registered.
items.prior_blocker: The observation is radius-dependent and uncertain; any stellar sphere is an explicitly idealized volume proxy, not a resolved 3D stellar surface.

items.name: Oort Cloud volume
items.decision: Existing procedural theoretical cloud has synthetic sample positions and an assumed outer boundary. It fails the hard rule; no exact public 3D population boundary acquired.
items.prior_blocker: The 50,000 AU spherical boundary is a theoretical convention, not a measured shell; a boundary diagram must be labeled as such.

items.name: Orion Nebula volume
items.decision: Existing Length Orion geometry includes image-based authored depth. It is not an observed 3D density boundary or imported source mesh; no Volume reuse under the hard rule.
items.prior_blocker: Projected emission maps do not uniquely determine depth; a 3D volume model needs distances and a defined nebular boundary.

items.name: Milky Way disk volume
items.decision: Existing NASA concept image/Length procedural galaxy does not establish a measured density cutoff and 3D disk boundary for the selected volume. No conversion of a 2D image to invented depth.
items.prior_blocker: The disk volume depends on chosen radial and vertical extents; require a sourced 3D stellar-density field and a declared cutoff.

items.name: Local Group volume
items.decision: Existing public member coordinates do not define the selected enclosing spherical boundary; its enlarged project-authored galaxy glyphs cannot supply an enclosed group volume.
items.prior_blocker: A spherical volume depends on a chosen Local Group radius/boundary; member positions alone do not define a filled volume.

items.name: Virgo Supercluster volume
items.decision: Existing 2MRS member positions are a galaxy catalog, not an observed surface of the selected spherical volume convention. No arbitrary hull/shell generated.
items.prior_blocker: The supercluster boundary is definition-dependent; a spherical proxy should not be presented as a mapped matter volume.

items.name: Observable universe volume
items.decision: Existing WMAP Length visualization includes an authored spherical cutaway/horizon guide. Observed angular CMB temperatures do not supply a directly measured solid boundary; no reuse under this round hard rule.
items.prior_blocker: This is a derived spherical cosmological volume, not a solid surface model; a scale diagram would be illustrative rather than observed geometry.
